title: The test that failed after 8pm
situation: During my co-op at Northwind Labs, an integration test failed about once a week and the team had started re-running it until it passed.
task: I offered to find out why, since re-running hid any real failures.
action: I logged the inputs on every failure and saw they all happened after 8pm Eastern. The test built the current date in local time while the server compared in UTC. I switched the test to a fixed UTC clock and wrote up the cause in the pull request.
result: The test stopped failing for the rest of my term, and the team stopped re-running CI by habit. I did not measure time saved.
questions: Tell me about a bug you are proud of fixing.
Tell me about a time you took initiative.

title: Keeping keyboard support in Shelfmate
situation: Two weeks before our capstone demo, my teammate wanted to cut keyboard support from the shelf board to save time.
task: One book club member navigated with a keyboard only, so I wanted to keep it without risking the demo.
action: I proposed a two-day timebox. I replaced our custom focus handling with the browser's own focus order and added tests with Testing Library.
result: Keyboard support shipped in a day and a half and the demo went ahead on time.
questions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.
How do you handle a deadline?

title: The demo that crashed on a double swap
situation: At our first Shelfmate demo, two people swapped the same book at the same time and the app recorded both.
task: Fix it before the club started using the app the next week.
action: I moved the swap into one PostgreSQL transaction that checks the book is still available, and added a test that sends two swaps at once.
result: No double swaps were reported during the term the club used it. I now test the two-tab case before I demo anything that writes data.
